Whomever Mahādeva Śambhu desires to protect on his own,
to him instantly comes knowledge born of the Self, free from egoism.
I am not able again to perform worship of this teacher of the universe;
I surrender myself and go to Śaṃkara for refuge."
Thus Viṣṇu meditated upon Śiva, his consciousness fixed on praise.
By the true grace of the lord of spirits, he was raised up again to the earth.
And I wandered in the sky for many years;
with dizzy eyes and slackened wings, I became exhausted,
and higher and higher I saw the fire standing before me,
a pillar of fire resembling a massive liṅga, Śiva's splendor worshipped by gods.
Some perfected ones, born from parts of that splendor, seeing [me], said:
"To me, who have made effort, desirous to see the eternal, highest limit of Śambhu—
oh, this one truly wishes to practice foolishness even today!
Even with the fall of his body imminent, his egoism indeed has not departed.

1.1.m:
His wings shattering, exhausted, his eyes bewildered,
this delusion regarding the boundless splendor will prove useless.
In this way Janārdana, in the form of a boar, his mind bewildered,
was turned back by Śiva alone, who possesses unconditioned compassion.
Crores of gods like Brahmā and the rest arise
from the atomic particles of that splendor whose limit he desires to see.
The Lord Śiva, who is attained by meditating on one's own Self,
if he gives understanding to him in due time, his egoism will perish."
Hearing these compassionate words of those perfected ones as they spoke thus,
my egoism shattered, I thought within myself:
"Not from knowledge of the multitude of Vedas, nor from austerity, nor from visiting sacred fords,
does knowledge of Śiva arise, except by his own grace.
Though my pair of wings is shattered, though my firm body sinks down,
my mind is eager once again to maintain its own egoism.
Fie on me, overcome by egoism, unaware of my own lack of power!

1.1.m:
Constant salutation to the perfected ones whose minds are dedicated to Śiva,
by whose association, through acquired austerity, my intellect is purified,
so that I recognize this Śiva standing before me as the cause of my own Self;
endowed with the power obtained through whose grace,
all the gods will continuously have their enemies subdued;
whose ultimate reality the Vedas do not know through great Āgamas—
to that very Śambhu, distinct from the universe, I go for refuge."
Then, having addressed the lotus-eyed Viṣṇu, I said—
he who had regained his form and resorted with devotion to Śiva, who bears the moon on his crest:
"Ah, what wonder is this that has come upon us, who are full of valor,
that we resorted to egoism, which was produced by Śambhu!
Hearing of the vast and great battle between the two of us,
that very Śaṃkara, of immeasurable soul, took away all the egoism
of both of us by revealing his own greatness.

1.1.m:
Obeisance to the venerable Gaṇeśa.
Now begins the first half of the glorious Aruṇācalamāhātmya.
With the triple mark of ashes upon his forehead, wearing a musk mark on his brow, wearing a gleaming garland, his loins clad in a radiant loincloth, / bearing on his head the unassailable king of serpents and the crescent of the moon, the yogin of Aruṇagiri, a light unto all, reigns supreme. (1)
Vyāsa said:
Then the sages dwelling in the Naimiṣāraṇya said to Sūta: / “We wish to hear from you the māhātmya of Aruṇācala. (2)
Tell us that māhātmya!” Addressed thus, Sūta said to those sages:
Sūta said:
Long ago, Sanaka questioned the four-faced [Brahmā] for this very purpose. (3)
Listen with attentive minds; I shall tell it to you now, / for hearing it with devotion destroys the sins of men. (4)
Once in Satyaloka, seated before Brahmā who sits on the lotus, / Sanaka bowed low and, standing with joined palms, questioned him: (5)
Sanaka said:
“O support of the worlds, lord of gods, you who are known through the Vedas, four-faced one! / Complete knowledge arose in me through your grace. (6)
When the mirror of my mind was purified through the glory of devotion to you, / all knowledge was reflected there simply upon a single teaching. (7)
The essential meaning of the Vedas and what is known through the Vedas—the undisturbed knowledge of Śiva— / I have fully attained through your glances, O teacher of the universe! (8)
There are Śiva’s liṅgas on earth: divine ones, O treasury of compassion, / and human ones, those established by siddhas, and elemental ones, O leader of the gods. (9)
Tell me of that pure, divine liṅga that possesses the majesty of destroying enemies, / self-manifest in Jambudvīpa, fiery in nature. (10)
Tell me, O treasury of mercy, of that which destroys sin by the mere recollection of its name, / and eternally grants conformity to Śiva’s form! (11)
That imperishable splendor of Śiva which is the beginningless support of the universe, / and seeing which one becomes fulfilled—let that be taught to me!”
Thus hearing the word of that devoted [disciple], full of curiosity, (12)

And remaining seated on the lotus, the four-faced one meditated long on Śambhu, / his mind plunged into the ocean of inner bliss. (14)
When he saw Śiva consisting of a pillar of fire, as seen in ancient times, / which transcends every support, he was aware of nothing else. (15)
Then, to carry out the command received once more from Śiva, / the lord withdrew his heart from yoga and remembered his bowed son. (16)
His body bristling with horripilation born of the darśana of Śiva, / his eyes filled with tears of joy, he spoke in a choked voice: (17)
Brahmā said:
“Therefore, my son, I was reminded of ancient times by you; / while contemplating Śiva’s yoga, I remembered [you] out of affection for you. (18)
Supreme devotion to Śiva has arisen in you through your many austerities; / by that, my heart was, as it were, turned back in an instant. (19)
By their deeds those whose devotion to Sadāśiva increases at all times / purify the entire world, O untroubled one! (20)
Conversation, cohabitation, sporting, mingling, / darśana of the devotees of Śiva, and remembering them, destroys evil. (21)
Listen to the wondrous, divine light named Aruṇādri, / full of spontaneous compassion, as it appeared in former times. (22)
Both I and Nārāyaṇa were born from the manifestation surpassing all, / from Sadāśiva who was unfolding the resolve: ‘May I become many.’ (23)
Arisen according to [our] nature, we quarreled with one another; / and fighting with pride, we were never fatigued. (24)
Beholding the terrible enthusiasm for battle between the two of us, / Īśvara, the embodiment of compassion, then thought: (25)
‘Why has this fight, which will destroy the worlds, arisen between these two / who have entered into a dispute: “It was created by me,” “I am the protector”? (26)
At this moment, being myself visible to these two who are utterly bewildered, / if I do not stop the battle, the destruction of the worlds will take place.’ (27)”

1.1.m:
"My greatness is heard in the Vedas as transcending all. / These two deluded ones, their memory lost through anger, do not know it.
Every creature considers itself exceedingly superior. / But the fool who does not acknowledge the equality or superiority of others falls downward.
If in any world I give a measure of myself, / then, from realizing that form, he too may attain measure of the Self."
Deciding thus in his mind, Sadāśiva himself / arose as a pillar of fire between the two of us as we fought,
surpassing all the worlds, blazing on every side like fire.
Then, because it had neither beginning nor end, they stood with eyes pained, / their resolve broken upon seeing that blazing pillar of fire.
And before us a bodiless voice arose: / "Why is a battle undertaken, you two children of foolish mind?
Śiva alone will judge the difference between your powers. / This form standing here, composed of a pillar of fire, belongs to Śambhu.
If you two see its beginning and end, [that one is] superior in power." / Hearing those words, the two of us then ceased from combat,
and I and Viṣṇu, who possesses movement, resolved to search it out. / That form composed of a pillar of fire belonging to Śambhu was devoid of beginning or end;
the two of us resolved to inspect it from its beginning and its end. / Just as two children wish to seize the moon reflected in the sky,
so the two of us set out to measure that great splendor. / Then Viṣṇu, with great zeal, became a boar of immense body,
and to seek its base he tore open the interior of the earth. / And I, having assumed the state of a wild gander, flying up with great speed,
desirous to see its crown, plunged upward into the sky. / Rending the entire earth lower and lower, Mādhava
beheld the pillar of fire as if appearing from below. / Though searching for many crores of years,
not seeing the imperishable beginning of the splendor, he became afflicted in form and distressed.

With the rings of his tusks shattered, his joints and sinews giving way, / afflicted with exhaustion, overcome with thirst, Hari was unable to go on.
Unable to sustain that incomparable boar-like form, / exhausted even from turning back, the lord of Ramā despaired.
Endowed with an immeasurable soul, his body utterly fatigued, / his glory departed, exhausted by effort, taking refuge in Śiva who is worthy of refuge, he thought:
"Fie on this great delusion of mine born of egoism, / by which I did not recognize my master, my own Self!
For he is the root of all the Vedas, of the gods, and of the worlds; / he is Śiva in person—how could there be a root to him?
From him alone, who is devoid of beginning and end, have I arisen. / That I began to search for Śiva, having assumed an animal's body, [was folly].
By the grace of Father Śambhu, a friend of unconditioned compassion,
Brahmā said:
Then I, chanting the Vedas with all my mouths, praised Śiva,
having performed mental worship filled with devotion: 1.
“Homage to the great Śiva, the sole cause of all worlds,

This splendor pervading the universe shines perpetually;

O Lord of the gods, this [form] of yours shines like a mirror. 5.

there is no other apart from me, who also dissolves in what consists of you. 6.
An atom, if it is the recipient of your compassion, surely attains greatness;
there is none higher beyond you, nor beyond me, because of relying upon that. 7.
The mind dedicated to you expects no separation from you.
How could speech proceed in singing your glory? 8.

Having addressed this with humility, bowing again and again,

1.1.m: Sovereignty, mastery, good fortune, and the deception of death—

By granting all bodily limbs, by destroying all diseases,
and by bestowing all desires, be visible on the surface of the earth.
Saying, ‘So be it,’ to the boon-granting god, Śiva, the lord of Aruṇādri,
the Lord of Kamalā bowed down and prayed, speaking thus:
‘Be gracious, O Lord full of compassion, Lord of the Crimson Mountain!
O Maheśa whose rise is manifest for the welfare of all worlds!
Since, taking refuge in you, I am capable of protecting the world
and have attained the status of Lord of Śrī, therefore may they become your devotees.
This great and wondrous form of yours cannot be worshipped by those of little merit,
whose foot and crown could not be seen by me or by Brahmā.
Those mortals who worship you with circumambulations, prostrations,
dances, songs, and acts of veneration, have attained their goal, freed from sin.
Those men who worship you with fasts, observances, sacrificial sessions,
offerings, and rituals—may they become universal monarchs.
For those making a grove, a pavilion, and a well purified according to rule,
in your presence, O Lord of Aruṇādri, may there be no rebirth!
One who circumambulates by prostrating bodily, endowed with the eight supernatural powers,
is instantly freed from all sins, with a purified mind.
We two also never abandon your lotus feet;
[you] are to be meditated upon by all men who have come into your presence.’
Granting the boon, ‘So be it,’ to Viṣṇu, the moon-crested god,
in the form of Aruṇācala, assumed the state of an immovable liṅga.
This liṅga made of fire, the sole cause of all the worlds,
famed as Aruṇādri, is seen on the surface of the earth.
Even at the time of the dissolution of the world, when the four oceans are agitated
and the ends of the worlds are submerged, the nearby ground around it remains untouched.
Filling the three worlds with raindrops as massive as elephants,
the great clouds such as Puṣkara rest upon its peak.
When the dissolution of the elements begins, in the involution of primal nature,
all the seeds of the future remain securely preserved in this place.
And from the brahmins serving its feet, summoned by me
again after the dissolution, the collection of Vedic study is recovered.
Of all the sciences, arts, treasures of scriptures,
āgamas, and Vedas, the true preservation is found here.
Sages of praiseworthy vows, dwelling within its caves and caverns,
with matted hair, shine with the brilliance of ten million suns and fires.

Sadāśiva, whose nature is primordial sound, is mounted on the pedestal of the letter ‘A’.
He who is ever worshipped by the guardians of the eight directions through eight liṅgas,
as the Eight-formed Lord, is the bestower of the eight supernatural powers.
Where siddhas and the lords of the gods, having left their own realms,
and having abandoned the golden mountain [Meru], dwell expecting liberation.
Thus the fruition of the collected merits of the earth,
famed as the red mountain [Aruṇādri], grants boons to the devotees of his devotees.
By hosts of gods arrived from Kailāsa and the peak of Meru,
Śambhu, in the form of the Crimson Mountain, giver of all boons, is worshipped."

Hearing this speech of his, the god of gods, the Grandfather [Brahmā],
the embodiment of compassion, bowing to the Lord of Aruṇādri, spoke:
Brahmā said:
"Listen, my child, to that ancient deed of Pārvatī,
how she attained tranquility by taking refuge in the Lord of Aruṇādri.
Once Mahādeva, the husband of Pārvatī, approached
a divine jeweled lion-throne adorned with jeweled archways,
charming with wish-fulfilling trees bearing jeweled flowers and fruits,
inlaid with most precious gems, with hung pearl canopies,
having the great fragrance of divine incense and heaps of scattered flowers,
thronged with bees buzzing in networks of dangling garlands,
where the mount of Guha [the peacock] danced to the deep sound of divine musical instruments,
where great elephants were terrified by the movement of Pārvatī’s lion,
with apsarases only dancing and singing,
whose courtyard was attended [by all], served by the guardians of the directions,
with excellent sages praising him with mantras born from the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas,
surrounded by celestial seers, gods, siddhas, and royal seers,
and by gaṇas of diverse forms whose bodies were adorned with sacred ashes,
radiant with the wearing of rudrākṣas, full of devotion to Śiva,
with the sounds arising from the triple symphony of vīṇā, flute, mṛdaṅga, and other instruments,
charming with the ringing of bells mixed with the sound of the Vedas.
The Lord, companion of Pārvatī, adorned that charming,
exceedingly divine throne out of desire to favor his devotees,
assuming his spotless, auspicious form consisting of all fiery splendor.
Together with Ambikā, the glorious one, an ocean of compassion, disported
with music, diverse tales, and varieties of dice-play;
with the grotesque dances of the gaṇas, he delighted Pārvatī.
Having dismissed all the gods, the seers, and the members of the assembly,
and having granted various desired boons to the world of devotees,
amid wonderful traditions and flowers of all seasons,
he disported together with Umā among rows of jeweled palaces,
at delightful step-wells with flights of jeweled steps,
on the peaks of pleasure-mountains, inside groves of golden plantains;
with the gentle wind, cool with the waves of the Gaṅgā
and smelling of blooming lotuses, his fatigue from sport removed,
of his own will, the god himself delighted his beloved,
the auspicious goddess, the embodiment of love, beautiful with all good fortune.
Once in secret, the affectionate, innocent [goddess],
knowing her lover to be obedient to her command, approached him respectfully from behind,
and with both her lotus-like hands, the three eyes of the teacher of the universe,
of Śambhu, she playfully covered, wondering in curiosity: 'What is this?'
When the eyes in the form of the moon, sun, and fire were covered one by one,
a terrifying darkness descended there for a long time.
In half a blink of the God's eye, tens of millions of years passed.
Through the darkness born of the Goddess's play, the destruction of the universe took place.
The universe was filled all around with boundless darkness.
Devoid of the movement of light, it fell into destruction.

Gautama said:
Formerly in a kalpa, Nārāyaṇa was reclining upon the ocean of waters;

"Alas, how dreadful is this form of darkness, deluding the universe,
by which Viṣṇu does not wake even now, though the kalpa has ended!
Even the gods do not see the complete person of light;
how then could reflective minds obtain peace from the darkness?"
Having so resolved in their minds, they meditated upon the God of gods, Umā's lord,
dwelling within themselves, the mass of fiery splendour, free from taint.
Then the blessed Maheśvara, the mass of fiery splendour, was pleased,
entreated for the protection of the universe by the bowed eternal seers.
Then, from Śambhu who consists of fire, arising as rays of sparks,
the thirty-three crores of gods sprang forth.

"Out of an excess of darkness, I slept at an improper time;

1.1.m: The Gaṅgā staying at the base, the Yamunā abiding in the sky,
and the river born from the Moon upon the summit, attend upon the Crimson Mountain.
Many sacred fords also arose on all sides;
in ancient times, Mārkaṇḍeya was not able to know their distinctions.
By means of many austerities, he satisfied the Lord of the Crimson Mountain,
and from him who was pleased, that lord of sages requested a boon:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
“O Blessed Lord, Lord of Aruṇādri, thousands of different sacred fords
are celebrated and shine forth, but are difficult to understand for those of little wit.
How can mortal men attain [their] presence in a single place on earth?
For serving each of them separately is inadequate [for humans].
You whose brilliance is hidden within, who are approached by all the gods—
act in such a way for those who fear touching the Crimson Mountain.”
And I, having worshipped Śambhu on Mount Aruṇa through austerity,
worshipped the subtle liṅga for the benefit of the entire world.
A divine aerial chariot fashioned by Viśvakarman, with various festivals,
he conceived, and again produced all perpetual enjoyments.
The eminent sages obtained various treatises on righteousness;
endowed with devotion, they performed all the rites of Śiva.
And by me, having worshipped Śambhu, offerings produced in the fire were made,
Seven fair-hipped maidens were assigned for the worship.
In ancient times, by kings who had slain host of enemies and regained their kingdoms,
The Lord of the Red Mountain was worshipped individually with diverse offerings.
This wondrous wealth of direct experience, removing distress, this Śiva-liṅga in the form of a mountain,
Flawless, whose name cannot be fully reached, this supreme Lord of the Aruṇa mountain—worship him!
Suited to protect people bowed in reverence, dispelling all defilements by its mere remembrance,
Attain, O fortunate one, supreme devotion to Aruṇagiri through the combination of immeasurable heaps of merit!

1.1.m:
Pārvatī said:
How did the liṅga made of fire become accessible on earth?
How did it attain pacification for all living beings as well?
How did the sacred fords arise from the holy Aruṇa Mountain?
Or tell me, how did the mountain withdraw all its limbs?
Gautama said:
In the Kṛta age, the mountain was made of fire; in the Tretā age, it was a mountain of gems;
In the Dvāpara age, it was a mountain of gold; in the Kali age, it is an emerald mountain.
When it stood made of fire extending for many yojanas in the Kṛta age,
The great seers performed circumambulation on the outside, and it grew calm.
Gradually, the glorious Lord of the Aruṇa mountain was pacified when beseeched by the gods;
For the protection of the world, Aruṇācala became exceedingly calm.
Then Gaurī said to the sage: "How was Aruṇācala pacified?
Or how did the thirty [gods] pray to this Lord of gods?"
Hearing her words, Gautama then spoke,
Praising her matchless devotion that knows the true meaning of reality.
Gautama said:
In ancient times, being unable to approach the mountain that was in the form of fire,
The gods formerly offered praise, having worshipped with products of sacrifice:
"O Lord, Ruler of the Aruṇa mountain, bringing welfare to all the worlds!
Though in the form of fire, shine forth pacified on the surface of the earth!
'He who is copper-colored, ruddy, brown, and supremely auspicious,'
Thus all the Vedas praise you whose form is Śiva.
Salutations to the copper-colored, ruddy Śiva, the Supreme Self,
Whose nature is to be known through the Vedas, who is Soma, who is bliss incarnate!
All this universe, moving and unmoving, is your form, O God;
This is seen as the treasure of the gods, like your own form.
When the rain clouds pour and numerous torrents flow,
The consumption of water by fire at the end of an age is proper for you.
Water arose from fire, indeed from you, the Supreme Self;
Out of the glory of your wondrous qualities, it spreads the creation of the universe.
Become cool, O Mahādeva, O Śoṇācala, ocean of mercy!
Become accessible to all living beings, O Lord!"
Praised thus by all the bowed gods, the lover of devotees,
The Lord, instantly becoming cool, became approachable.
Again, rivers and torrents with abundant water began to flow;
Even when the clouds poured down, he did not swallow up much water.
Even so, having a splendor equal to billions of rising morning suns and fires of time,
He became accessible to living beings.
Emitting the waters of the universe and filling the rivers with flowing streams,
The God shines forth everywhere at all times.
Those various sacred fords arose all around through the prayer
Of the guardians of the directions, the gods, and the great-souled seers.
Brahmā said:
Hearing his words, Gaurī, filled with curiosity,
Proceeded to hear about the origin of all the sacred fords.
Pārvatī said:
Which sacred fords arose from Śoṇādri for the protection of the world?
Lord, tell me the entire origin of the sacred fords.

1.1.m:
Hearing her words, which he had heard from the Lord of Mountains in the past,
He began to explain the origin of all the sacred fords.
Gautama said:
The great sacred ford named Aindra arose in Indra's direction.
Bathing there in ancient times, Śakra cast off the sin of killing a brahmin.
The divine sacred ford Brahmatīrtha arose in the corner of fire [the south-east].
Having bathed here, Agni abandoned the sin resulting from union with another's wife.
The great sacred ford named Yāmya spreads in Yama's direction [the south].
Bathing here, Yama cast away the fear arising from the Brahmā-weapon.
The great sacred ford Nairṛta shines in the south-western direction.
Bathing there, seers attained victory over ghosts and vetālas.
In the western direction shines the sacred ford Vāruṇa.
Bathing here in ancient times, Varuṇa recovered his own quiver of darts.
In the north-west shines the sacred ford Vāyavīya here.
Bathing there, Vāyu attained the glory of being the life-breath of the world.
And in the northern direction here, it is remembered as Somatīrtha.

In ancient times, O goddess, Mārkaṇḍeya prayed to Śaṃkara:
"O Sadāśiva, O Mahādeva, God of gods, Lord of the world!
May there be an assembly of many sacred fords together in one place here.
By what means, O Lord? Tell me with grace, O Śaṃkara!"
Hearing his words, the God of gods, the Lord of Umā,
With a pleased mind revealed the means to the sage.
Maheśvara said:
"Always at the time of the offering, the confluence of all sacred fords,
Having arrived in my presence, serves me in a hidden form.
You need seek no other sacred ford here, O great sage;
At the time of my offering, the collection of sacred fords is seen.
Therefore, with devotion, the assembly of all sacred fords
Should be viewed by the sages and by all the gods at the conclusion of the food offering."

Vows, sacred fords, austerities, Vedas, sacrifices, observances, and so forth,

Hearing the speech of the best of sages, the daughter of the king of mountains, being pleased,
said: "Most wondrous is this network of sacred fords upon the earth taught here by you.
I have attained my goal, O best among those who practice tapas, through meeting you; now the network of sacred fords

I questioned the Lord of Aruṇādri, full of compassion, as I bowed:
'This form consisting of fire, the Great Lord, cannot be approached;
how can I now worship him with rites fit for the mortal world?
Or how can I carry out this command meaningfully?
O glorious one, teach me the means whereby you may be approachable.'
When thus petitioned, the glorious god, the Lord of Śoṇācala,
the Self of all, a treasury of compassion, showed grace to me as I bowed:
'I will manifest subtle liṅgas upon the surface of the earth;
perform my worship through the various rituals prescribed in the Āgamas.
With the powers of your tapas, worship my wondrous, subtle liṅga,
surrounded by five enclosures and named the Lord of Aruṇādri.'
Having thus instructed, the Great God Śiva, the self-manifest, pure, and vast,
revealed his form to me in the shape of a subtle liṅga.

Remember [also] the other divine names declared in the Purāṇas.
Worship me especially and constantly by circumambulation (pradakṣiṇa), / 16

1.1.m: There is no rebirth for him who makes the circumambulation
of the One whose form is the Red Mountain; he surely attains eternal permanence. // 34
The entire earth is purified by the touch of his foot-dust,
who places a single step in circumambulating the Lord of the Red Mountain. // 35
Bowing in every direction, meditating, praising with folded hands,
not touching his hands with anyone, he should make the circumambulation slowly. // 36
Just as a woman close to childbirth walks without agitation,
so should one make the circumambulation, not even hearing the sound of his footsteps. // 37
Bathed, wearing pure garments, adorned with ashes and rudrākṣa beads,
absorbed in the remembrance of Śiva, the wise person should step slowly. // 38
Reflecting on the collision, excessive jostling, and blocking of the path
of the mantras moving in front, and of thousands of gods,
and of invisible Siddhas and others having the form of wind,
the wise devotee should place his foot gently, in an agreeable manner. // 40
Or else, loudly chanting the names of Śiva with excellent songs
and performing the dance of Śiva, he should circumambulate together with the devotees. // 41
Or listening to my māhātmya with an undivided mind and with reverence,
filled with the nectar of bliss, he should circumambulate slowly. // 42
And with various gifts, meritorious deeds, and acts of assistance to those in need,
filled with compassion according to his ability, the faithful person should go round. // 43
One should meditate upon it as a liṅga composed of fire in the Kṛta age, as a mountain of jewels in the Tretā,
as golden in the Dvāpara, and as an emerald mountain in the Kali age. // 44
Or meditating upon its form as crystal, red and self-luminous,
freed from all sins, he goes to the city of Śiva. // 45
Because it cannot be reached by speech and mind, because it is self-incommensurable,
and because of its fiery nature, meditating upon this supreme liṅga named the Unattainable Mountain,
I am easily reached by the one who performs the circumambulation.
His foot-dust causes men to become ageless and immortal. // 47
Whosoever assumes a single form in circumambulating the Lord of the Red Mountain—
the vehicles of the hosts of gods pray to one another
to bear the foot of those performing the circumambulation of the Red Mountain.
The celestial trees such as the wish-fulfilling tree provide shade
for mortals on earth who are performing the circumambulation of the Red Mountain.
Surrounded by thousands of gods, Gandharvas, and others,
hundreds of millions of aerial chariots crowded with attendants wait upon
those who make my circumambulation on earth, with the dust of their feet. // 51
The great pathway is purified; seen, it bestows the state of Śiva.
Performing circumambulation with one’s whole body rolling, one attains a heavenly form in an instant.
Having attained an adamantine body, he cannot be overpowered on the earth.
The gods, keen on aerial journeys, the siddhas, and the supreme seers,

Seeing modesty and devotion toward me during the course of circumambulation,
they, filled with joy, grant boons to mortals.
Here, in ancient times, the thirty-three gods, having performed circumambulation,
residing daily along the path, individually attained the status of ten million.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Bestowal of Boons Establishing the Supreme Preeminence of Aruṇācala by Śiva," in the first half of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya in the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. // 13
The first half of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya is complete.
Thus ends the first half of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya. (3.1)
Now begins the first half of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya in the third Māheśvarakhaṇḍa. (1-3-1)

1.1.s: 1 naimiṣāraṇyavāsibhirmunibhiḥ sūtamaharṣiṃ pratyaruṇācalamāhātmyaśravaṇecchayā pṛṣṭe sūtena tānpratyaruṇācalamāhātmyakathanopakrame brahmasanakasaṃvādakathanam, sanakena taijasaśivaliṅgamāhātmyaśravaṇecchayā pṛṣṭena bhagavatā brahmaṇā'ruṇācaleśvarataijasaśivadhyānapū-rvakamaruṇācaleśvaramāhātmyakathanopakramavarṇanam, tatra pūrvaṃ viṣṇubrahmaṇoḥ parasparamātma-śraiṣṭhayaprāgalbhyapūrvakaṃ yudhyamānayormadhye vahnistambhamayabhagavadāvirbhāvaḥ, ākāśavāṇyā ca tayoryuddhādviratiḥ, atha tasyāgnistambhamayarūpasyā'nādyantasya bhagavato'dho'ntaṃ paricchettuṃ viṣṇorvarāharūpeṇa gatasyā'nantasyāntaṃ paricchettumaśakyatayā viṣādaprāptyanantaraṃ pūrvasthalaṃ pratyāgamanama, ūrdhvamantaṃ paricchettuṃ brahmaṇo haṃsarūpeṇa gatasyā'nantasyāntaṃ paricchettumaśakyatayā viṣādaśaptyanantaramūrdhvalokasthitānāṃ siddhānāṃ vacanato'nantasyānantatāṃ parijñāya pūrvasthalaṃ prati sametya bhagavataḥ purato'vasthitivarṇanam..... ..... 214
1.1.d: 1 नैमिषारण्यवासिभिर्मुनिभिः सूतमहर्षिं प्रत्यरुणाचलमाहात्म्यश्रवणेच्छया पृष्टे सूतेन तान्प्रत्यरुणाचलमाहात्म्यकथनोपक्रमे ब्रह्मसनकसंवादकथनम्, सनकेन तैजसशिवलिङ्गमाहात्म्यश्रवणेच्छया पृष्टेन भगवता ब्रह्मणाऽरुणाचलेश्वरतैजसशिवध्यानपू-र्वकमरुणाचलेश्वरमाहात्म्यकथनोपक्रमवर्णनम्, तत्र पूर्वं विष्णुब्रह्मणोः परस्परमात्म-श्रैष्ठयप्रागल्भ्यपूर्वकं युध्यमानयोर्मध्ये वह्निस्तम्भमयभगवदाविर्भावः, आकाशवाण्या च तयोर्युद्धाद्विरतिः, अथ तस्याग्निस्तम्भमयरूपस्याऽनाद्यन्तस्य भगवतोऽधोऽन्तं परिच्छेत्तुं विष्णोर्वराहरूपेण गतस्याऽनन्तस्यान्तं परिच्छेत्तुमशक्यतया विषादप्राप्त्यनन्तरं पूर्वस्थलं प्रत्यागमनम, ऊर्ध्वमन्तं परिच्छेत्तुं ब्रह्मणो हंसरूपेण गतस्याऽनन्तस्यान्तं परिच्छेत्तुमशक्यतया विषादशप्त्यनन्तरमूर्ध्वलोकस्थितानां सिद्धानां वचनतोऽनन्तस्यानन्ततां परिज्ञाय पूर्वस्थलं प्रति समेत्य भगवतः पुरतोऽवस्थितिवर्णनम्..... ..... 214
1.1.m: 1. When the sages dwelling in the Naimiṣāraṇya, wishing to hear the Aruṇācalamāhātmya, question the great seer Sūta, Sūta, beginning his narration of the Aruṇācalamāhātmya to them, recounts the dialogue between Brahmā and Sanaka; description of how the venerable Brahmā, questioned by Sanaka who wished to hear the glory of the fiery Śivaliṅga, began the narration of the glory of the Lord of Aruṇācala preceded by meditation upon the fiery Śiva, the Lord of Aruṇācala; there, previously, as Viṣṇu and Brahmā were fighting each other out of arrogance regarding their own superiority, the manifestation of the Lord in the form of a pillar of fire between them; and their cessation from battle due to an incorporeal voice; then, in order to determine the lower end of that Lord who was in the form of a pillar of fire and without beginning or end, Viṣṇu, having gone in the form of a boar, unable to determine the end of the endless one, meets with despondency and returns to the previous place; in order to determine the upper end, Brahmā, having gone in the form of a swan, unable to determine the end of the endless one, meets with despondency, but having learned from the words of the perfected beings stationed in the upper world the endlessness of the endless one, comes back to the previous place and stands before the Lord. 214

1.1.s:
2 atha brahmaviṣṇubhyāṃ vahnistambhamayasya bhagavataḥ stavanam, tato vahnistambhamayaparameśvareṇa
brahmaviṣṇvorvarapradānama, vrahmaviṣṇvoḥ prārthanayā vahnistambhamayena parameśvareṇa nijarūpamupasaṃhṛtyāruṇācalarūpeṇa sthāvaraliṃgatādhāraṇama, sthāvaraliṃgamāhātmyavarṇanam 25
1.1.d:
2 अथ ब्रह्मविष्णुभ्यां वह्निस्तम्भमयस्य भगवतः स्तवनम्, ततो वह्निस्तम्भमयपरमेश्वरेण
ब्रह्मविष्ण्वोर्वरप्रदानम, व्रह्मविष्ण्वोः प्रार्थनया वह्निस्तम्भमयेन परमेश्वरेण निजरूपमुपसंहृत्यारुणाचलरूपेण स्थावरलिंगताधारणम, स्थावरलिंगमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् 25
1.1.m: 2. Next, the praise of the Lord in the form of a pillar of fire by Brahmā and Viṣṇu; then, the granting of boons to Brahmā and Viṣṇu by the Supreme Lord in the form of a pillar of fire; at the request of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the Supreme Lord who was in the form of a pillar of fire withdraws his own form and assumes the state of an immovable liṅga in the form of Aruṇācala; description of the glory of the immovable liṅga. 25

1.1.s: 3 athāruṇādrīśvaracaritravarṇanama, tatra bhagavatyā jagadambayā kadācidrahasi śambhoḥ krīḍāvaśena netratrayapidhānama, śaṃkarasya candrasūryāgnirūpeṣu triṣu netreṣu pārvatyā nimiṣārdhamātraṃ pihiteṣu sakalajagato'kāle kṣayaḥ, tadānīmavināśibhistapasā labdhasphūrtibhiḥ siddhaistapobalaprāptajñānacakṣuṣā tatsāṃbaśaṃkaracaritraṃ vijñāya sāṃbasadāśivastutikaraṇama, śrīśaṃkareṇa siddhānāṃ stutimākarṇya nijanimiṣārdhena vatsarakoṭiparimitakālātikramaṇena jagataḥ pralayaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārvatīṃ pratīdaṃ tvayā'yogyaṃ karma kṛtamityukte pārvatyā svakṛtajagatkṣayajanitaduritanivṛttyai prāyaścittapṛcchāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ bhagavatā lokaśikṣārthaṃ pārvatyai tapaḥkaraṇārthamanujñākaraṇam, tataḥ śrīśaṃkarānujñayā pārvatyāḥ kāṃcīpurīsthakaṃpānadītīrasthitaikāmratale tapaścaryārthamāgamanam.
1.1.d: 3 अथारुणाद्रीश्वरचरित्रवर्णनम, तत्र भगवत्या जगदम्बया कदाचिद्रहसि शम्भोः क्रीडावशेन नेत्रत्रयपिधानम, शंकरस्य चन्द्रसूर्याग्निरूपेषु त्रिषु नेत्रेषु पार्वत्या निमिषार्धमात्रं पिहितेषु सकलजगतोऽकाले क्षयः, तदानीमविनाशिभिस्तपसा लब्धस्फूर्तिभिः सिद्धैस्तपोबलप्राप्तज्ञानचक्षुषा तत्सांबशंकरचरित्रं विज्ञाय सांबसदाशिवस्तुतिकरणम, श्रीशंकरेण सिद्धानां स्तुतिमाकर्ण्य निजनिमिषार्धेन वत्सरकोटिपरिमितकालातिक्रमणेन जगतः प्रलयं दृष्ट्वा पार्वतीं प्रतीदं त्वयाऽयोग्यं कर्म कृतमित्युक्ते पार्वत्या स्वकृतजगत्क्षयजनितदुरितनिवृत्त्यै प्रायश्चित्तपृच्छायां कृतायां भगवता लोकशिक्षार्थं पार्वत्यै तपःकरणार्थमनुज्ञाकरणम्, ततः श्रीशंकरानुज्ञया पार्वत्याः कांचीपुरीस्थकंपानदीतीरस्थितैकाम्रतले तपश्चर्यार्थमागमनम्.
1.1.m: 3. Next, narration of the deeds of the Lord of Aruṇādri; therein, the venerable Mother of the Universe, out of sport, once covers the three eyes of Śambhu in secret; when the three eyes of Śaṃkara, which are in the forms of the moon, the sun, and fire, are covered by Pārvatī for merely half a twinkling of an eye, the untimely destruction of the entire universe; then, the indestructible perfected beings, whose vigor was gained by austerity, perceiving that deed of Śaṃkara accompanied by Ambā with the eye of knowledge attained through the power of austerity, sing praises to Sadāśiva accompanied by Ambā; Śrī Śaṃkara, hearing the praise of the perfected beings and seeing the dissolution of the universe caused by the passing of a period of ten million years during his half a twinkling of an eye, says to Pārvatī: “An improper deed has been committed by you”; upon Pārvatī asking for an expiation to ward off the evil arising from the destruction of the universe caused by herself, the Lord grants permission to Pārvatī to perform austerity for the instruction of the world; then, by the command of Śrī Śaṃkara, Pārvatī’s arrival to perform austerity beneath a mango tree situated on the bank of the Kampā river in the city of Kāñcī.

1.1.s: 4 atha kampānadītīrasthitaikāmratale pārvatyā saikataśivaligaṃ saṃsthāpya, svadharmācaraṇapūrvakaṃ tapaścaryākaraṇam, atha śaṃkareṇa pārvatyā dṛḍhabhaktiparīkṣaṇārthaṃ nadīpūrapravāheṇa samaṃtato vyāptau kṛtāyāṃ devyā saikataśivaliṃgasya pravāhāllayabhītyā dṛḍhamāliṃgya pūrapravāheṇa veṣṭyamānayā'pi liṅgaṃ vihāyā'nyato'gamanam, pārvatīdṛḍhaparirambhaṇataḥ saikataliṅge pārvatīkucacūcukacihnamudrāṅkitatvavarṇanam, athākāśavāṇyā pārvatīmāśvāsya tasya saikataliṃgasyābhyarhaṇe varaṃ pradāyāruṇācalaṃ prati gatvā gautamopadeśena tapaḥkaraṇārthamanujñākaraṇam, atha devyā pārvatyā tatra kaṃpānadītīre darśanārthaṃ sevārthaṃ cāgatebhyaḥ sarvadevebhya ṛṣibhyaśca saikataśivaliṅgapūjanārthamājñākaraṇam, tataḥ pārvatyāḥ sarvadevaiḥ sahāruṇādrau gautamamaharṣerāśramaṃ prati gamanam- 218 2
1.1.d: 4 अथ कम्पानदीतीरस्थितैकाम्रतले पार्वत्या सैकतशिवलिगं संस्थाप्य, स्वधर्माचरणपूर्वकं तपश्चर्याकरणम्, अथ शंकरेण पार्वत्या दृढभक्तिपरीक्षणार्थं नदीपूरप्रवाहेण समंततो व्याप्तौ कृतायां देव्या सैकतशिवलिंगस्य प्रवाहाल्लयभीत्या दृढमालिंग्य पूरप्रवाहेण वेष्ट्यमानयाऽपि लिङ्गं विहायाऽन्यतोऽगमनम्, पार्वतीदृढपरिरम्भणतः सैकतलिङ्गे पार्वतीकुचचूचुकचिह्नमुद्राङ्कितत्ववर्णनम्, अथाकाशवाण्या पार्वतीमाश्वास्य तस्य सैकतलिंगस्याभ्यर्हणे वरं प्रदायारुणाचलं प्रति गत्वा गौतमोपदेशेन तपःकरणार्थमनुज्ञाकरणम्, अथ देव्या पार्वत्या तत्र कंपानदीतीरे दर्शनार्थं सेवार्थं चागतेभ्यः सर्वदेवेभ्य ऋषिभ्यश्च सैकतशिवलिङ्गपूजनार्थमाज्ञाकरणम्, ततः पार्वत्याः सर्वदेवैः सहारुणाद्रौ गौतममहर्षेराश्रमं प्रति गमनम्- 218 2
1.1.m: 4. Next, Pārvatī, having installed a sand Śivaliṅga beneath the mango tree on the bank of the Kampā river, performs austerity in accordance with her own duty; then, when Śaṃkara, in order to test Pārvatī’s firm devotion, causes a flood of the river to swell on all sides, the goddess, fearing the destruction of the sand Śivaliṅga by the current, embraces it firmly and, though surrounded by the current of the flood, does not abandon the liṅga to go elsewhere; description of the sand liṅga being imprinted with the mark of Pārvatī’s nipples due to Pārvatī’s tight embrace; then, an incorporeal voice, comforting Pārvatī and granting a boon for her worship of that sand liṅga, grants permission to go to Aruṇācala and perform austerity according to the instruction of Gautama; then, the goddess Pārvatī gives an order to worship the sand Śivaliṅga to all the gods and seers who had come to the bank of the Kampā river for darśana and service; then, Pārvatī’s departure together with all the gods to the hermitage of the great seer Gautama on Aruṇādri. 218 2

1.1.s: 5 atha gautamamaharṣiṇā pārvatyāḥ svāgatasatkārakaraṇam, pārvatāprārthitena gautamamaharṣiṇā pārvatīṃ pratyaruṇācalamāhātmyavarṇanam-tatprasaṃgena brahmapuṣkaramāhātmyavṛttāntavarṇanam 220 1
1.1.d: 5 अथ गौतममहर्षिणा पार्वत्याः स्वागतसत्कारकरणम्, पार्वताप्रार्थितेन गौतममहर्षिणा पार्वतीं प्रत्यरुणाचलमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्-तत्प्रसंगेन ब्रह्मपुष्करमाहात्म्यवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् 220 1
1.1.m: 5. Next, the welcoming and hospitality shown to Pārvatī by the great seer Gautama; the great seer Gautama, requested by Pārvatī, describes the glory of Aruṇācala to Pārvatī; in that context, the narration of the account of the glory of the Brahmapuṣkara. 220 1

6. A detailed narration of the glories of the various sacred fords established on Aruṇācala by the host of all the gods beginning with Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, by the host of great seers, and by the host of royal seers. 221 2

1.1.s: 7 athāgnimayasya liṅgasya pārvatyopaśāntatākāraṇe pṛṣṭe gautamamaharṣiṇā'ruṇācaleśvarasya caturyugīyanāmabhedavarṇanam tatra devakṛtastutyāruṇācaleśvarasya bhagavataḥ śītalatāprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, athāruṇācalasthāṣṭalokapālasthāpitāṣṭadiksthatīrthamāhātmyavṛttāntaḥ, mārkaṇḍeyaprārthanayā maheśvareṇa sarvatīrthasamuccayasyaikīkaraṇavarṇanam, atha tīrthamāhātmyaṃ śrutvā suprasannayā pārvatyā śrīparameśvarārcanavidhijijñāsayā gautamamaharṣiṃ prati praśnakaraṇam. .. .... 224 1
1.1.d: 7 अथाग्निमयस्य लिङ्गस्य पार्वत्योपशान्तताकारणे पृष्टे गौतममहर्षिणाऽरुणाचलेश्वरस्य चतुर्युगीयनामभेदवर्णनम् तत्र देवकृतस्तुत्यारुणाचलेश्वरस्य भगवतः शीतलताप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, अथारुणाचलस्थाष्टलोकपालस्थापिताष्टदिक्स्थतीर्थमाहात्म्यवृत्तान्तः, मार्कण्डेयप्रार्थनया महेश्वरेण सर्वतीर्थसमुच्चयस्यैकीकरणवर्णनम्, अथ तीर्थमाहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा सुप्रसन्नया पार्वत्या श्रीपरमेश्वरार्चनविधिजिज्ञासया गौतममहर्षिं प्रति प्रश्नकरणम्. .. .... 224 1
1.1.m: 7. Next, when Pārvatī asks the reason for the cooling down of the fiery liṅga, the great seer Gautama describes the different names of the Lord of Aruṇācala across the four ages; therein, the account of the venerable Lord of Aruṇācala attaining coolness through the praise performed by the gods; next, the account of the glory of the sacred fords situated in the eight directions, established by the eight guardians of the worlds residing at Aruṇācala; description of the unification of the assembly of all sacred fords by Maheśvara at the request of Mārkaṇḍeya; then, Pārvatī, exceedingly pleased upon hearing the glory of the sacred fords, puts a question to the great seer Gautama wishing to know the procedure for worshipping the Supreme Lord. 224 1

8. Next, the great seer Gautama, having related his own story concerning the grace of Śrī Śaṅkara, the Lord of Śoṇādri, describes in detail the glory of the worship of Śiva, the Lord of Aruṇācala, as proclaimed in the Āgama spoken by Śrī Śaṃkara. 225 1

1.1.s: 9 śrīśaṃkareṇa śrīśoṇādrīśvaravividhanāmakathanam, atha śoṇādrīśvarapradakṣiṇāmāhātmya- kathanam, śoṇādrīśvarapradakṣiṇāmāhātmyaprasaṃgena dharmaketurājavṛttāntavarṇanam, bhagavate vividhopacārasamarpaṇamāhātmyavarṇanam, gautamena svasmai bhagavatā bhagavatyā apītaku- cākhyāyāḥ pārvatyāstapodīkṣāgrahaṇāya svasamīpaṃ pratyāgamanādibhaviṣyadvṛttāntaṃ varṇa- yitvā bhagavatyāḥ pārvatyāḥ praśaṃsākaraṇam ,tataḥ pārvatyā tapaḥ kartuṃ gautamenānumoditayā gautamāśrame kācitparṇaśālāmadhyāsya yathoktaniyamapūrvakaṃ tapaścaryākaraṇavarṇanam 226
1.1.d: 9 श्रीशंकरेण श्रीशोणाद्रीश्वरविविधनामकथनम्, अथ शोणाद्रीश्वरप्रदक्षिणामाहात्म्य- कथनम्, शोणाद्रीश्वरप्रदक्षिणामाहात्म्यप्रसंगेन धर्मकेतुराजवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, भगवते विविधोपचारसमर्पणमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, गौतमेन स्वस्मै भगवता भगवत्या अपीतकु- चाख्यायाः पार्वत्यास्तपोदीक्षाग्रहणाय स्वसमीपं प्रत्यागमनादिभविष्यद्वृत्तान्तं वर्ण- यित्वा भगवत्याः पार्वत्याः प्रशंसाकरणम् ,ततः पार्वत्या तपः कर्तुं गौतमेनानुमोदितया गौतमाश्रमे काचित्पर्णशालामध्यास्य यथोक्तनियमपूर्वकं तपश्चर्याकरणवर्णनम् 226
1.1.m: 9. The recitation of various names of the venerable Lord of Śoṇādri by Śrī Śaṃkara; next, the proclamation of the glory of circumambulating the Lord of Śoṇādri; in connection with the glory of circumambulating the Lord of Śoṇādri, the narration of the account of King Dharmaketu; description of the glory of offering various articles of worship to the Lord; Gautama’s praise of the venerable Pārvatī after narrating the future event concerning himself, told by the Lord, namely the arrival of the venerable Pārvatī, named Apītakucā, into his presence to receive initiation into austerity; then, description of Pārvatī, encouraged by Gautama to perform austerity, dwelling in a certain leaf-hut in Gautama’s hermitage and performing austerity according to the prescribed observances. 226

1.1.s: 10 atha tatra tapasyantīṃ devī prati mahiṣāsuratrastānāṃ sarveṣāmindrādidevānāmāgamanam, indrādidevairdevyai mahiṣāsurakṛtanijavitrāsanivedanama, devānāṃ dainyamālokya devyā mahiṣāsuravadhārthaṃ pratijñāṃ kṛtvā devānāmāśvāsanakaraṇam, devīta āśvāsanaṃ prāpya deveṣu gateṣu satsu devyā svātmanaḥ paritaścaturṣu dikchaileṣu sthānarakṣārthaṃ caturbaṭukasthāpanam, tathā ca catasṛṇāṃ nijaparicārikāṇāmaruṇādriṃ prati kevalamatithipreṣaṇārtha- mājñākaraṇam, evaṃ vyavasthāṃ kṛtvā gautamāśramasaṃnidhau pārvatyāstapaḥkaraṇam, pārva- tītapaḥsāmarthyāttatrāśrame sarvataḥ śāntatāvarṇanam; atha kadācinmahiṣāsurasya mṛgayārthaṃ śoṇādriparisare bhramaṇam, atha devīsthāne baṭubhirniruddhena mahiṣāsureṇa vṛddhā- tithibrāhmāṇarūpeṇa devīṃ prati gatvā nijapraśaṃsākaraṇapūrvakaṃ svavaraṇārthaṃ svābhiprāyanivedanam, atha devyā mahiṣāsuraṃ prati yuddhārthaṃ nijābhiprāyakathanam, tato yuddhodyataṃ mahiṣāsuraṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyārūpāyāstasyā jagadaṃbāyā bhavyabhayaṃkaradurgārūpeṇāvasthānam, mahiṣāsureṇa nijasenāhvānam, brahmādidevairdevyai vividhanijāyudhasamarpaṇam, devīsva- rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayena palāyitaṃ mahiṣāsuraṃ prati devyā vānaramukhasuragurudvārā'ruṇācalaṃ pratyāgantuṃ niṣeddhuṃ sandeśapreṣaṇam, suraguruproktaṃ devīsaṃdeśaṃ niśamya bhṛśaṃ kruddhena mahiṣāsureṇāruṇācale devyā saha yuddhārthaṃ sarvadaityasainyapreṣaṇam, āgataṃ daityasainyaṃ vilokya devyā svatejasā vividhabhūtavetālamātṛkāyoginyādigaṇānāṃ sṛṣṭikaraṇam, daityasainyadevīsainyayoḥ pracaṇḍayuddhavarṇanam, tatra yuddhe mahiṣāsureṇa saha devyā yuddhārambhaḥ. 229 1
1.1.d: 10 अथ तत्र तपस्यन्तीं देवी प्रति महिषासुरत्रस्तानां सर्वेषामिन्द्रादिदेवानामागमनम्, इन्द्रादिदेवैर्देव्यै महिषासुरकृतनिजवित्रासनिवेदनम, देवानां दैन्यमालोक्य देव्या महिषासुरवधार्थं प्रतिज्ञां कृत्वा देवानामाश्वासनकरणम्, देवीत आश्वासनं प्राप्य देवेषु गतेषु सत्सु देव्या स्वात्मनः परितश्चतुर्षु दिक्छैलेषु स्थानरक्षार्थं चतुर्बटुकस्थापनम्, तथा च चतसृणां निजपरिचारिकाणामरुणाद्रिं प्रति केवलमतिथिप्रेषणार्थ- माज्ञाकरणम्, एवं व्यवस्थां कृत्वा गौतमाश्रमसंनिधौ पार्वत्यास्तपःकरणम्, पार्व- तीतपःसामर्थ्यात्तत्राश्रमे सर्वतः शान्ततावर्णनम्; अथ कदाचिन्महिषासुरस्य मृगयार्थं शोणाद्रिपरिसरे भ्रमणम्, अथ देवीस्थाने बटुभिर्निरुद्धेन महिषासुरेण वृद्धा- तिथिब्राह्माणरूपेण देवीं प्रति गत्वा निजप्रशंसाकरणपूर्वकं स्ववरणार्थं स्वाभिप्रायनिवेदनम्, अथ देव्या महिषासुरं प्रति युद्धार्थं निजाभिप्रायकथनम्, ततो युद्धोद्यतं महिषासुरं दृष्ट्वा कन्यारूपायास्तस्या जगदंबाया भव्यभयंकरदुर्गारूपेणावस्थानम्, महिषासुरेण निजसेनाह्वानम्, ब्रह्मादिदेवैर्देव्यै विविधनिजायुधसमर्पणम्, देवीस्व- रूपं दृष्ट्वा भयेन पलायितं महिषासुरं प्रति देव्या वानरमुखसुरगुरुद्वाराऽरुणाचलं प्रत्यागन्तुं निषेद्धुं सन्देशप्रेषणम्, सुरगुरुप्रोक्तं देवीसंदेशं निशम्य भृशं क्रुद्धेन महिषासुरेणारुणाचले देव्या सह युद्धार्थं सर्वदैत्यसैन्यप्रेषणम्, आगतं दैत्यसैन्यं विलोक्य देव्या स्वतेजसा विविधभूतवेतालमातृकायोगिन्यादिगणानां सृष्टिकरणम्, दैत्यसैन्यदेवीसैन्ययोः प्रचण्डयुद्धवर्णनम्, तत्र युद्धे महिषासुरेण सह देव्या युद्धारम्भः. 229 1
1.1.m: 10. Then, the arrival of all the gods headed by Indra, terrified of the demon Mahiṣa, before the Goddess as she was performing austerity there; the report made by the gods headed by Indra to the Goddess concerning their terrorization by the demon Mahiṣa; seeing the misery of the gods, the Goddess taking a vow to slay the demon Mahiṣa and consoling the gods; after receiving consolation from the Goddess and when the gods had departed, the Goddess stationing four youths (baṭukas) on the hills in the four directions around herself for the protection of the place; and likewise giving orders to her four female attendants solely to send guests toward Aruṇādri; having made such an arrangement, Pārvatī's performance of austerity in the vicinity of Gautama's hermitage; the description of universal tranquility in that hermitage through the power of Pārvatī's austerity; then, once upon a time, the demon Mahiṣa wandering in the environs of Śoṇādri for hunting; then, the demon Mahiṣa, having been blocked by the youths at the Goddess's place, going toward the Goddess in the form of an old brahmin guest, and stating his intention to choose her [in marriage] while singing his own praises; then the Goddess declaring her intention to fight the demon Mahiṣa; then, seeing the demon Mahiṣa intent on battle, the Mother of the Universe, who was in the form of a maiden, assuming the grand and terrifying form of Durgā; the demon Mahiṣa summoning his army; the offering of their various personal weapons to the Goddess by the gods headed by Brahmā; the Goddess sending a message via the monkey-faced preceptor of the gods (Bṛhaspati) forbidding the demon Mahiṣa, who had fled in terror upon seeing the form of the Goddess, to come back toward Aruṇācala; hearing the Goddess's message spoken by the preceptor of the gods, the demon Mahiṣa, highly enraged, dispatching the entire Daitya army to fight with the Goddess at Aruṇācala; seeing the arriving Daitya army, the Goddess creating through her own splendor various hosts of bhūtas, vetālas, mātṛkās, yoginīs, and others; the description of the fierce battle between the Daitya army and the Goddess's army; therein, the commencement of the Goddess's battle with the demon Mahiṣa. 229 1

1.1.s: 11 devīmahiṣāsurayoryuddhe devyā mahiṣāsuramardanama, atha mahiṣārdinyā durgāyā indrādidevaiḥ stutikaraṇam, atha mahiṣāsuraśiraḥsthitaśivaliṃgasya devyāḥ pāṇitalaṃ āsañjanavarṇanam, tataḥ svahastena śivabhaktahananaṃ jātamiti manyamānāyā jagadambāyāḥ śokena gautamāgratastīrthayātrārthakasvasaṃkalpanivedanam, tato gautamena jagadambāyā āśvāsanapūrvakaṃ mahiṣāsuravṛttakathanapūrvakaṃ gauryai doṣanivṛttyarthamaruṇācalāgratastīrtha snānarūpopāyakathanam.. -... - -... -. -. -. 231 2
1.1.d: 11 देवीमहिषासुरयोर्युद्धे देव्या महिषासुरमर्दनम, अथ महिषार्दिन्या दुर्गाया इन्द्रादिदेवैः स्तुतिकरणम्, अथ महिषासुरशिरःस्थितशिवलिंगस्य देव्याः पाणितलं आसञ्जनवर्णनम्, ततः स्वहस्तेन शिवभक्तहननं जातमिति मन्यमानाया जगदम्बायाः शोकेन गौतमाग्रतस्तीर्थयात्रार्थकस्वसंकल्पनिवेदनम्, ततो गौतमेन जगदम्बाया आश्वासनपूर्वकं महिषासुरवृत्तकथनपूर्वकं गौर्यै दोषनिवृत्त्यर्थमरुणाचलाग्रतस्तीर्थ स्नानरूपोपायकथनम्.. -... - -... -. -. -. 231 2
1.1.m: 11. In the battle between the Goddess and the demon Mahiṣa, the crushing of the demon Mahiṣa by the Goddess; then, the praising of Durgā, crusher of Mahiṣa, by the gods headed by Indra; then, the description of the Śivaliṅga situated on the demon Mahiṣa's head clinging to the palm of the Goddess's hand; then, the Mother of the Universe, thinking that the slaying of a devotee of Śiva had occurred by her own hand, expressing out of grief before Gautama her resolve to go on a pilgrimage; then Gautama consoling the Mother of the Universe, narrating the conduct of the demon Mahiṣa, and telling Gaurī the remedy for the removal of the sin in the form of bathing in the sacred ford before Aruṇācala. 231 2

1.1.s: 12 athākāśavāṇyā gauryā svakhaḍgena khaḍgatīrthaṃ nirmāya tatra kārtikamāsaparyaṃtaṃ nimajjanam, khaḍgatīrthatīre svahastacyutamahiṣāsuraśiraḥsthitaliṃgasthāpanama, tataḥ kārtike māsi kṛttikānakṣatre'ruṇādrīśvarastutikaraṇam, tataḥ prasannena bhagavatā'ruṇādrīśvareṇa jyotīrūpeṇāvirbhūya jyotirantargatahiraṇmayapuruṣarūpeṇa jagadaṃbāyai varapradānam, tato jagadambayā'ruṇādrīśvarasya pradakṣiṇākaraṇam, tataḥ prasannena śrīśoṇādrīśvareṇa śaṃkareṇa bhagavatā saha jagadaṃbāyāḥ samāgamavarṇanam ......... 233 1
1.1.d: 12 अथाकाशवाण्या गौर्या स्वखड्गेन खड्गतीर्थं निर्माय तत्र कार्तिकमासपर्यंतं निमज्जनम्, खड्गतीर्थतीरे स्वहस्तच्युतमहिषासुरशिरःस्थितलिंगस्थापनम, ततः कार्तिके मासि कृत्तिकानक्षत्रेऽरुणाद्रीश्वरस्तुतिकरणम्, ततः प्रसन्नेन भगवताऽरुणाद्रीश्वरेण ज्योतीरूपेणाविर्भूय ज्योतिरन्तर्गतहिरण्मयपुरुषरूपेण जगदंबायै वरप्रदानम्, ततो जगदम्बयाऽरुणाद्रीश्वरस्य प्रदक्षिणाकरणम्, ततः प्रसन्नेन श्रीशोणाद्रीश्वरेण शंकरेण भगवता सह जगदंबायाः समागमवर्णनम् ......... 233 1
1.1.m: 12. Then Gaurī, in accordance with a voice from the sky, creating the Khaḍgatīrtha with her sword and bathing there until the month of Kārtika; the installation on the bank of the Khaḍgatīrtha of the liṅga situated on the head of the demon Mahiṣa that fell from her hand; then, in the month of Kārtika under the asterism of Kṛttikā, the offering of praise to the Lord of Aruṇādri; then the Lord of Aruṇādri, pleased, manifesting in the form of light and, in the form of a golden person within the light, granting a boon to the Mother of the Universe; then the Mother of the Universe circumambulating the Lord of Aruṇādri; then the description of the union of the Mother of the Universe with the pleased Lord Śaṃkara, the Lord of Śoṇādri. 233 1

1.1.s: 13 atha śivena pārvatyai varapradānapūrvakaṃ pārvatyā saha raṃtukāmyayā pārvatyaṃge mṛgamadālepanam, mṛgamadotpattivṛttāntavarṇane pulakākhyadaityasya caritrasthanam, devīhastotthitakamalasya vṛttāntaḥ, tatprasaṃgena kāñcīsthamahādevamāhātmyavarṇanapūrvakapārvatīdarśanamāhātmyavṛddhaye pārvatyāḥ śivaṃ prati prārthanā, śivena pārvatyai varapradānam, aruṇādrīśvaramahāvaibhavamāhātmyavarṇanam. -... -. - - 235 1
1.1.d: 13 अथ शिवेन पार्वत्यै वरप्रदानपूर्वकं पार्वत्या सह रंतुकाम्यया पार्वत्यंगे मृगमदालेपनम्, मृगमदोत्पत्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णने पुलकाख्यदैत्यस्य चरित्रस्थनम्, देवीहस्तोत्थितकमलस्य वृत्तान्तः, तत्प्रसंगेन काञ्चीस्थमहादेवमाहात्म्यवर्णनपूर्वकपार्वतीदर्शनमाहात्म्यवृद्धये पार्वत्याः शिवं प्रति प्रार्थना, शिवेन पार्वत्यै वरप्रदानम्, अरुणाद्रीश्वरमहावैभवमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्. -... -. - - 235 1
1.1.m: 13. Then Śiva, granting a boon to Pārvatī, anointing Pārvatī's body with musk out of a desire to make love with Pārvatī; in the narration of the origin of musk, the account of the deeds of the Daitya named Pulaka; the episode of the lotus that sprang from the Goddess's hand; in that connection, Pārvatī's prayer to Śiva for the enhancement of the māhātmya of seeing Pārvatī preceded by the description of the māhātmya of Mahādeva situated in Kāñcī; Śiva granting a boon to Pārvatī; the description of the māhātmya of the great majesty of the Lord of Aruṇādri. 235 1
